chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who arrives as a pilgrim and the heat becomes intense upon him, so he performs Tawaf by the Kaaba and delays the Sa'i until it cools. He said: 'There is no problem with it, and sometimes I do it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to delay Sa'i after Tawaf in Hajj to avoid heat?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the principle of *rukhas* (concessions) in Shia jurisprudence, demonstrating that the strict sequence of Hajj rituals can be adapted for physical necessity, such as extreme heat. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) not only permits delaying Sa'i but also cites his own practice, reinforcing the validity of this variation within the school of Ahl al-Bayt. This underscores the flexibility of ritual law when balancing spiritual obligation with human well-being.
